newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK REVISED CPI CLOSER TO TRUE INFLATION-OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: GREEK REVISED CPI CLOSER TO TRUE INFLATION-OFFICIAL.

text.p: Greece's revised CPI index is a better indicator of the true cost of living and produces more accurate inflation figures, an official at the National Statistics Service (NSS) told Reuters.

"By construction, the revised CPI index is a better index of the true cost of living," said the NSS official. "The Greek CPI index is a version of the Laspeyres price index that we all know that it suffers from the base year effect."
Consumer price inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December using 1994 for base year.
Inflation would have been 7.1 percent year-on-year in January under the previous CPI index using 1988 for base year. It stood at 7.5 percent in December.

The Laspeyres price index weights the prices by quantities in the base year and overestimates the rise in the cost of the original standard of living. The degree of overestimation depends on how far away the price index for the current year is from the base year.
The Paasche price index, another type of price index used for CPI construction, underestimates the rise in the cost of living.

"Other EU countries use chain-indexes for calculating consumer price inflation that push the base year forward in order to avoid this problem (overestimation)," he said. "Unfortunately we are not in a position to do this right now." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
